questions.question_text: To convert an area from ha to $\text{m}^2$, what must you do?

options.why: Reversed the direction; a square metre is smaller than a hectare, so the count goes up.
Used the length factor $100$ without squaring it for the two dimensions.
Used the square kilometre factor $1000^2$ in place of the hectare factor $100^2$.

questions.solution_text:
A square metre is smaller than a hectare, so the conversion multiplies.
$1\text{ ha} = 100\text{ m} \times 100\text{ m}$
Multiply by $100^2 = 10\,000$.

questions.question_text:
Which is the larger area, $0.62\text{ m}^2$ or $5800\text{ cm}^2$?
Give the larger area in $\text{cm}^2$.

options.why: Converted $0.62\text{ m}^2$ using the factor $1000$ to get $620\text{ cm}^2$ and chose the other area.
Multiplied $0.62$ by the length factor $100$ instead of by $100^2$.
Multiplied $0.62$ by $1\,000\,000$, using the square kilometre factor.

questions.solution_text:
$0.62\text{ m}^2 \times 100^2$
$= 6200\text{ cm}^2$
$6200 > 5800$, so the area given in $\text{m}^2$ is larger.
$6200\text{ cm}^2$

questions.question_text:
A student converts an area from $\text{mm}^2$ to $\text{cm}^2$ by dividing by $10$, because there are $10$ mm in a centimetre.
What should the student divide by?

options.why: Kept the length factor, ignoring that a square centimetre is $10$ mm along each of two sides.
Cubed the length factor $10$ instead of squaring it for a two-dimensional measure.
Used the metre-to-centimetre area factor $100^2$ instead of the centimetre-to-millimetre one.

questions.solution_text:
A square centimetre is $10$ mm along each of two sides.
$10 \times 10 = 100$, so $1\text{ cm}^2 = 100\text{ mm}^2$.
The student should divide by $100$.

questions.question_text:

options.why: Converted the courtyard using the factor $1000$, getting $54\,000\text{ cm}^2$ before dividing.
Converted the courtyard using the length factor $100$, getting $5400\text{ cm}^2$ before dividing.
Converted the courtyard using $1000^2$, the square kilometre factor, before dividing.
